blind_spots.blind_spot: On-orbit edge processing is pitched as solving bandwidth by 'transmitting only actionable results' but the pack never addresses what happens when the downlink itself goes denied/intermittent for the ground segment receiving those results.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A DDIL ground segment means the 'actionable result' sits unsent in the same way raw data would have — the architecture assumes a reliable downlink exists at exactly the moment it matters, the same blind spot as the 30fps crowd-detection case, just one hop further down the chain.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is optimizing the space-side compute problem (SWaP, edge inference) and has not yet had a ground-side DDIL failure force the redesign.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "transmitting only actionable results and information to the end-user"

blind_spots.blind_spot: GENIE's on-orbit 'user-defined data collection & processing tasks' implies mid-mission reprogramming of a DoD/MDA payload with zero mention of ATO, IL4/IL5, or STIG accreditation for that software pipeline.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A payload that can be arbitrarily reprogrammed on-orbit is exactly the kind of system an ISSO will refuse to grant an ATO for without a defined POA&M — this can stall a contract far longer than the hardware development itself.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company is hardware/mission-heritage focused (TRL-9 achieved, ISS flights) and hasn't yet hit the compliance wall that comes with operationalizing customer-defined software on a government payload.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "GENIE can perform countless user-defined data collection & processing tasks, cutting costs, latency & data volume"

blind_spots.blind_spot: The Phase I abstract title invokes 'Warfighter Training' but the entire pack contains no description of who trains on the system, how a non-engineer operator tasks the satellite, or what sustainment looks like once GENIEedge scales to a constellation.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without a defined training/CONOPS path, 'warfighter training' risks being a proposal keyword rather than a designed workflow — the same gap that kills adoption once a champion below flag-officer level has to actually operate it.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Small 9-14 person team is still in mission-heritage/demo mode (SEED, LIME, ATLAS pathfinders) and hasn't reached the phase where operator training becomes a forcing function.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: "A Proliferated, Low-Cost Satellite Platform for AI Software Development, Testing and Warfighter Training"

opener_hook: NOVI's SEED payload flew an MDA mission to the ISS this year — is the SP240's on-orbit reprogramming path already ATO'd for classified tasking?
what_they_do: Builds flight-proven on-board computers and AI-enabled smart satellites (GENIEedge) that process sensor data in orbit and downlink only the actionable intelligence.
